extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and applicants preparing/submitting NIH grant applications (faculty, postdocs, trainees) who want to understand or report award timelines
extracted.subtask_description: Collecting, reporting, and interpreting timelines and status-history milestones for NIH grant applications (A0/A1 etc.) from submission through Notice of Award, including JIT, council review, PO/GMS interactions, and common delays. Useful for applicants tracking or posting their award journey and reading eRA Commons status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include IC, activity code, and scores/percentiles when posting timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For those posting their timelines, since the whole thread is not carried along, please include the IC, funding activity code, and scores/percentiles along the way plus any useful advice, tips, cheerleading, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original guidance from the page: explicitly state the institute/center (IC), the funding activity code (e.g., R01, K99), and impact score/percentile at each relevant milestone so readers can compare similar applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report key eRA Commons status messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the standard eRA Commons status messages (e.g., 'Application entered into system', 'Scientific Review Group review pending', 'Scientific Review Group review completed', 'Summary Statement available', 'Council review completed', 'Pending administrative review', 'Award prepared: refer questions to Grants Management Specialist', 'Application awarded').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List dates for each status update; note that these messages are commonly cited in timelines and help interpret where an application is in the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report study section/Scientific Review Group (SRG) meeting dates and Summary Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the study section meeting date and the date the Summary Statement was made available (including impact score and percentile when provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, include reviewer comments/rebuttal requests and any post-review conversation with the Program Officer about the Summary Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify submission version (A0, A1, resubmissions) and timeline per version
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether a posted timeline is for an initial submission (A0) or a resubmission (A1, etc.) and give dates for each version’s milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many timelines span multiple submissions; recording which version corresponds to which status/score helps interpret eventual outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Just-In-Time (JIT) requests and responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Record dates and content of JIT notifications/requests (automated or personalized from GMS) and the dates JIT materials were submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note specific JIT items requested: IACUC/IRB approvals, Current & Pending Support, Institutional Support Letters, visa documentation, Clinical Trial milestones, data sharing or data records requests. Include JIT deadlines when posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Notice of Award (NOA) date and actual start date
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting award receipt, include the exact date of the Notice of Award (not just 'today') and the approved project start date (which may differ from proposed start date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly requests poster to 'include the date of the Notice of Award instead of just saying “today,” since the timestamp can get lost when the comment is archived.' Also note NIH can start awards earlier or later than proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report budget outcomes and percent cuts
rubrics_metrics.description: When awarded, report whether the budget was cut and by what percent (and whether modular vs. detailed budgets were used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters were asked to include '% people’s awards were cut' to help others plan how to reduce budgets in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Program Officer (PO) and Grants Management Specialist (GMS) interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Log dates and content of communications with Program Officers and Grants Management Specialists, including phone calls, emails, tailored PO requests, and advice (e.g., encouragement to resubmit, requests for rebuttal letters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly notes the importance of PO communication and that PO statements (e.g., 'cautiously optimistic') can inform expectations; include who said what and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: List typical administrative and programmatic delays and their causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Report contextual causes that affected timeline length (e.g., continuing resolution, federal budget timing, pandemics, IRB delays, visa/immigration documentation, internal budget issues, conversion between mechanisms, co-funding decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many timelines cite these as reasons for extended 'pending administrative review' periods or toggling between 'award prepared' and 'pending'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Council review and timing nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Include council meeting dates and the often separate 'Council review completed' status, and observe that council actions may occur before eRA Commons status updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page notes council review can be completed earlier than reflected in status pages; record both the actual council meeting date and the date the status changed, if known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret 'Pending administrative review' and 'Award prepared' phases
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize 'Pending administrative review' and 'Award prepared' as distinct administrative milestones that commonly precede NOA, and that their timing can be variable and sometimes toggles backward/forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters gave examples where 'Award prepared' reverted to 'Pending administrative review' due to budget or documentation issues; treat these as part of normal variability and report durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include IRB/IACUC and human-subjects/clinical-trial milestone reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Document dates for IRB/IACUC approvals and clinical-trial milestone submissions when relevant, since these often appear among JIT requests and can delay award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several timelines emphasized that IRB approval or human-subjects concerns caused significant additional time before award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record institutional/community administrative actions (e.g., rebuttals, tailored JIT, institutional letters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note when institutions submit rebuttal letters, institutional support letters, or tailored JIT items (e.g., proof of visa support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some POs requested rebuttal letters to be submitted before council; include submission dates and content summaries of such documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report unusual administrative events (mechanism conversions, co-funding, withdrawals)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is converted (e.g., R01 to R37), selected for co-funding (IDeA co-funding), or withdrawn because another version was funded, include these events and dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special events materially affect timelines and final outcomes and are repeatedly reported in the timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete timeline milestones to log
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical checklist of milestones to include: Application entered into system; SRG review pending; SRG review completed; Summary Statement available; Study section meeting date; Post-review PO conversation; Rebuttal letter; Council review completed; JIT requested/received; JIT submitted; Pending administrative review; Award prepared; Application awarded (NOA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page’s many examples implicitly establish this ordered milestone list; include exact dates for each when posting or analyzing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate impact of submission timing and institutional status (ESI, new investigator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report whether the applicant is Early Stage Investigator (ESI) or new investigator status and note how that affected funding chances or payline consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many posters noted ESI/early-stage status or institutional considerations (e.g., K12 protection) as relevant context for interpreting funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise about expectations and persistence (resubmission strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer applicant-oriented guidance: persistence matters, engage with mentors/POs, resubmit when advised, and address Summary Statement concerns thoroughly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contains repeated community advice and morale support: 'DO NOT GIVE UP!', 'communication with PO is important', and examples where multiple resubmissions eventually succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note reliability/lag of status updates across platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that status updates may appear on different ERA Commons pages at different times (status information page vs. status results page) and that emails/PO messages may not align exactly with eRA status timestamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters observed that updates sometimes populate on one page days before another and that the Commons is not always the definitive real-time indicator; record both system timestamps and human communications when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include contact points and who to refer questions to
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting statuses, include who to contact for questions at each stage: Scientific Review Administrator (SRG pending), Program Official (post-review, council), Grants Management Specialist (JIT/award prep).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page recurrently uses the recommended referral language printed in status messages; noting the correct contact clarifies next steps for others reading the timeline.
